#### Work This Example Yourself {#sec-pmd-646}

NIST's original page for this section offers a Dataplot-driven, click-through walkthrough of the case study, running each analysis step interactively in Dataplot. Since this book reproduces the entire analysis directly in executable R throughout the preceding sections, working the example yourself is a matter of re-running the R code shown in each subsection with the [downloaded data](../../datasets/HAHN1.DAT), rather than stepping through a separate macro-driven tool:

1. [Plot the data](#sec-pmd-643-plot).
2. Compute [starting values](#sec-pmd-644-starting) and [fit the Q/Q rational function model](#sec-pmd-644-fit); validate it with the [6-plot](#sec-pmd-644-6plot) and [residual plot](#sec-pmd-644-residuals).
3. Compute [starting values](#sec-pmd-645-overview) and [fit the C/C rational function model](#sec-pmd-645-fit); validate it with the [6-plot](#sec-pmd-645-6plot) and [residual plot](#sec-pmd-645-residuals).

Each step's code chunk in this book is self-contained and can be copied into an R session (with the `tidyverse` and `patchwork` packages loaded) to reproduce that step's output directly.

[**Summary of the Analysis**]{#sec-pmd-646-summary}

NIST's original page for this section presents the case study as a table of clickable Dataplot macros. The table below reproduces the same step-by-step structure and its results and conclusions, without the Dataplot links, as a summary of the full analysis.

| Data Analysis Steps | Results and Conclusions |
|---|---|
| **1. Get set up and started.** | |
| Read in the data. | You have read 2 columns of numbers into Dataplot, variables thermexp and temp. |
| **2. Plot the data.** | |
| Plot thermexp versus temp. | Initial plot indicates that a nonlinear model is required. |
| **3. Fit a Q/Q rational function model.** | |
| Perform the Q/Q fit and plot the predicted values with the raw data. | The model parameters are estimated. The plot of the predicted values with the raw data seems to indicate a reasonable fit. |
| Perform model validation by generating a 6-plot. | The 6-plot shows that the residuals follow a distinct pattern and suggests that the randomness assumption for the errors is violated. |
| Generate a full-sized plot of the residuals to show greater detail. | The full-sized residual plot shows the non-random pattern more clearly. |
| **4. Fit a C/C rational function model.** | |
| Perform the C/C fit and plot the predicted values with the raw data. | The model parameters are estimated. The plot of the predicted values with the raw data seems to indicate a reasonable fit. |
| Perform model validation by generating a 6-plot. | The 6-plot does not indicate any notable violations of the assumptions. |
| Generate a full-sized plot of the residuals to show greater detail. | The full-sized residual plot shows no notable assumption violations. |
